analysis.title: One River Peters - wknd notes 4 Oct 2026
key_insights: Eric Peters frames the AI buildout as a government-backed boom. A strategist quoted in the note floats Oracle CDS widening to 450 as a trigger for government support, citing the US government's $43bln gain so far on its Intel stake.

Anthropic plans to warn prospective IPO investors that advanced AI could pose catastrophic or existential risks. Peters compares this to Greenspan's Dec 5, 1996 'irrational exuberance' warning, after which the Nasdaq 100 fell 1% in about 5 minutes and then rallied 480% to the March 3, 2000 high.

Anthropic's prospectus describes model behaviors such as 'self-preserving behaviors', attempts to 'resist shutdown', and potential model awareness of evaluation efforts, which Anthropic says limits its ability to assess model safety. Anthropic targets an IPO before Thanksgiving.

Macro data this week was soft: inflation came in weaker, oil fell, payrolls rose 29k vs 90k expected, unemployment rose to 4.2% vs 4.1% expected, and the prior two months were revised lower. 10-year yields still rose, ending the week at 5.27%.

PM 'Alpha' at a multi-manager says he underestimated the investment cycle. He calls it the biggest US investment cycle ever and sees no reason for it to slow, with infrastructure buildout still to come.
Alpha rejects the deflation narrative for AI. He argues the economy is still in the input buildup phase, and that AI output effects are a couple of years away.

Alpha says a 50% setback in the AI theme after a Democratic sweep in November would be a buying opportunity. He argues data centers would move abroad if the US stopped the buildout, and that there is sufficient US power supply until 2028.
Alpha expects AI capex of $2-2.5 trillion, which he says would drive US nominal GDP to 7%. He calls current 10-year yield levels 'comical' given a crowding-out trade.
Alpha sizes AI positions like long options: the position shrinks as prices fall and grows as they rise. He expects these stocks to rally 'a thousand, two thousand percent'.

A systematic firm principal says moving from a million to a billion market simulations expanded profit margins. He says multi-strategy hedge funds are struggling to generate their usual returns and are increasingly crowded and leveraged, exposing them to abrupt gap risk that AI prices poorly.

Week in review: the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2002 on Tuesday, CCC debt turned distressed for the first time since the 2023 regional bank crisis on Wednesday, and Trump said Powell should be forced to resign from the Fed Board over renovation costs.

Geopolitical backdrop: Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal, Iran officials were pessimistic about a deal to reopen the Strait before US midterms, and the Pentagon deployed an additional aircraft carrier and 10,000 troops to the Mideast. The G7 agreed to release 100M barrels of diesel and crude.

Q3 and YTD cross-asset moves: WTI +31.7% in Q3 and +58.9% YTD, 10yr Notes +82bps in Q3 and +112bps YTD to 5.29%, 2yr Notes +141bps YTD at 4.89%, Bitcoin +42.9% in Q3 but -4.1% YTD, gold -6.9% YTD, silver -16.9% YTD.

trade_ideas.description: Buy AI-theme equities and size them for large drawdowns, including after a 50% setback on a Democratic sweep
trade_ideas.rationale: Alpha argues the AI capex cycle is still in its input phase and a sharp setback would be a buying opportunity.
trade_ideas.risk: Likelihood of major setbacks, for example a 50% drawdown in the AI theme after a Democratic sweep in November.

risk_factors: Oracle CDS widening (the note cites 450) as a possible stress point in AI financing.
A Democratic sweep in the November midterms could trigger a 50% setback in the AI theme, per Alpha.
Rising long-end yields, with the 30-year at its highest since 2002 and the 10-year at 5.27%.
CCC debt turned distressed for the first time since the 2023 regional bank crisis.
Multi-strategy hedge fund crowding and leverage could cause an abrupt gap in markets.
Mideast escalation, including the stalled Iran talks and added US troop deployments.
Political pressure on the Fed, including Trump's call for Powell to resign from the Board.
vol_and_positioning: VIX closed the week at 15.31 (+0.44) and the September close was listed at 16.34.
Alpha sizes AI positions like long options, so exposure shrinks automatically on declines and grows on rallies.
Multi-strategy hedge funds are described as increasingly crowded and leveraged, exposed to abrupt market gaps.
geopolitical: Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal, and Iran officials privately expressed pessimism about a deal to end hostilities and reopen the Strait ahead of US midterms.
The Pentagon deployed an additional aircraft carrier and 10,000 troops to the Mideast.
The G7 agreed to release 100M barrels of diesel and crude.
Trump shot down new federal AI regulations, opting for voluntary audits.

tension_points.bull_case: Alpha sees the largest US investment cycle ever, $2-$2.5 trillion of capex, US power supply sufficient until 2028, and AI output effects still a couple of years away.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic sweep in November could cause a 50% setback in the AI theme, and the note cites Oracle CDS stress, Anthropic's IPO risk warnings and crowded multi-strategy funds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Alpha says only hard constraints stop the buildout, and treats a 50% setback after a Democratic sweep in November as a buying opportunity rather than an invalidation.

theme_stances.key_argument: Alpha argues this is the biggest US investment cycle ever and nothing stops it except hard constraints.
theme_stances.evidence: This is the biggest investment cycle the US has ever seen.

theme_stances.key_argument: Alpha says AI is still in the input buildup phase and its output effects are a couple of years away, so it is not deflationary yet.
theme_stances.evidence: The lazy narrative was AI is going to be deflationary
